title: Async request context boundary and fanout safeguard
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Problem: We have intermittent cases where async/goroutine/fiber boundaries cause request-scoped tracing context to be lost when work is fan-out to background workers or queued systems. This results in orphaned spans, poor trace continuity across downstream services, and noisy error attribution in latency dashboards. Goal: implement a lightweight, cross-language-safe 'context boundary' pattern for SDKs and middleware that preserves a minimal carrier (trace ids, sampling decision, provenance stamps) across async boundaries and into background fanouts while keeping allocations and latency overhead minimal.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha: Drafted initial design on Confluence; proposed a two-layer envelope: (1) immutable carrier with trace_id, parent_id, sampling_hint, origin_stamp, ttl_ms and (2) optional local metadata for runtime hooks. Posted for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Context+Boundary+Design

2026-03-04 — Liam: Prototype for Node SDK using async_hooks showed a 3% p99 tail increase under microbench — changed approach to avoid async_hooks in hot paths; will use explicit attach/detach helpers and fast-path no-op when no fanout is detected.
2026-03-06 — Review feedback from SRE (Marta Singh): add metrics for context-loss-rate and span-orphan-rate, and ensure TTL prevents unbounded retention when enqueuing to work queues.

2026-03-09 — Engineering sync: Agreed on language-specific adapters: Node and Python will expose attachContext(handle) / detachContext(); Go will use context.Context wrapper with shallow copy-on-write for carrier. Added canary rollout plan tied to feature-flag 'ctx-boundary-v1'.

2026-03-11 — PR opened: GitHub PR #8471 implements carrier encode/decode and attach helpers for Node + tests — https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8471. Leaving a TODO to add Go and Python PRs after integration tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Context carrier implemented for Node, Python, and Go SDKs with identical canonical fields (trace_id, span_id, sampling_decision, origin_stamp, ttl_ms).
No regression in p50/p90/p99 tail latency beyond +5% in canary (measured on small internal traffic slice).
Metrics emitted: tracing.context_loss_rate, tracing.span_orphan_rate, instrumentation.overhead_ms per language. Dashboards updated and linked.
Canary rollout via feature flag: initial 5% services for 48 hours, followed by 25% then 100% if metrics within thresholds. Automated rollback if span_orphan_rate exceeds baseline + 2x.
Integration tests that simulate fanout to worker queues assert parent-child span linkage preserved across enqueue/dequeue.
